[TASK: 2560x1440 2K QHD 16:9 ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic 6x7 medium-format architectural survey photograph.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render razor-sharp ashlar courses, straight timber sash mullions, and crisp slate roofs.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the carriageway with authentic road surfacing, stone setts, whinstone kerbs, and clean flagstone pavements.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   The central communal pleasure grounds (Ainslie Place Gardens) feature mature broadleaf deciduous specimens:
- *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore maple) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common lime): Full, dense late-summer canopies displaying dark forest green foliage with early autumn margin chlorosis, dense branch massing, and lichen-mottled bark.
- *Ulmus glabra* (Wych elm) and *Prunus spinosa* understory: Full leafy crown structure consistent with early September phenology, maintaining canopy density prior to autumn leaf drop.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Pin-sharp infinite depth of field (f/11). Zero lens blur, tilt-shift, or depth-of-field falloff across foreground and background.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR LIGHT VECTOR (5400K Clean morning daylight with crisp directional shadows): Sun background upper-right (Azimuth 172.8°, Elevation 41.7°). backlit silhouettes with right rim lighting. shadows project forward toward lower-LEFT.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Medium format architectural documentary photograph of Ainslie Place, Edinburgh. Symmetrical curved Georgian crescent designed by James Gillespie Graham, featuring 3-storey, attic, and basement townhouses. Facades built in honey-buff fine-grained Craigleith quartz-arenite ashlar sandstone, featuring crisp V-jointed rustication on the ground floor, ashlar plat bands, moulded window architraves, running entablature, and a high blocking course. Rhythmic fenestration of white-painted timber 6-over-6 sash-and-case windows set into deep ashlar reveals. Cantilevered sandstone entrance platts span open basement lightwells, bounded by black painted cast-iron spearhead railings. Weathered Scottish slate roofs punctuated by massive ashlar chimney stacks with terracotta pots. Across the curving whinstone kerb line, the railed perimeter of Ainslie Place Gardens encloses mature Acer pseudoplatanus and Tilia × europaea trees with broad, dense canopies of dark green early-September foliage showing faint golden leaf-tip senescence. Clean, static urban composition completely devoid of vehicles, pedestrians, and street clutter, emphasizing sharp stone masonry, planar vertical accuracy, and precise Georgian neoclassical proportions. Straight perpendicular architectural survey framing.
